weather.tip: 92% rain chance tonight — carry an umbrella, avoid low-lying underpasses after dark, and budget extra time if you're heading out for dinner or a commute home.

around.headline: Cyber racket busted for using fake IAS, IPS profiles to dupe people
around.summary: Bengaluru police have busted a cyber racket that created fake profiles of IAS and IPS officers to cheat victims, per India Today. If a 'senior official' contacts you out of the blue on social media offering help or asking for money, verify their identity through the department's official website or helpline before responding.

around.headline: Man caught recording women during morning jog at Bengaluru lake
around.summary: A man was caught secretly recording women joggers at a Bengaluru lake, per The Times of India. If you spot someone filming without consent at a park or lake, alert on-site security or call 100 immediately rather than confronting them alone.

around.headline: Chairman's Club kitchen shut over hygiene violations
around.summary: Authorities shut the kitchen at Bengaluru's Chairman's Club after finding 40kg of expired chillies and mixed expired meat and vegetables, per NDTV, The Times of India and The Hindu. Before dining at any club or restaurant, check for a visible FSSAI licence and don't hesitate to ask staff about food storage if something looks off.
around.source: NDTV, The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: Two-wheelers banned on Bengaluru airport road; curbs on 3 flyovers
around.summary: Traffic police have banned two-wheelers on the road leading to Kempegowda International Airport and imposed curbs on three flyovers, per The Indian Express. If you ride a two-wheeler to the airport, check the diversion route in advance to avoid getting turned back at the barricade.

around.headline: Metro overcrowding to ease as CMRS clears new DTG trains
around.summary: The Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety has given the nod for new DTG trains on Namma Metro, which should ease overcrowding on busy stretches, per Deccan Herald. Regular riders on packed lines should see gradual relief as the new rakes are inducted.

around.headline: IMD red alert in Delhi for heavy rain; IGI Airport waterlogged
around.summary: The IMD has issued a red alert for heavy rain in Delhi, with severe waterlogging reported at IGI Airport, per Hindustan Times. If you have a flight to or from Delhi in the next couple of days, check your airline's status page before leaving for the airport.

events.name: Exhibition on women behind Bengaluru's buildings
events.note: A new exhibition spotlights the women architects and builders behind some of Bengaluru's landmark buildings, per Deccan Herald.

events.name: BMTC bus turned into a living portrait of the city
events.note: Artist Shubhang Ojha has turned a BMTC bus into a public artwork depicting the city, per homegrown.co.in — worth a look if you spot it on your route.

events.name: Wipro Bengaluru Marathon
events.note: Around 45,000 runners are expected — register soon if you want to run, and expect road closures on race day along the route.

events.name: Aero India 2027 registrations open
events.note: The first Aero India since Operation Sindoor will be held at Yelahanka Air Force Station; passes opened for registration this week.

street_smart.title: You've been chatting for a couple of weeks with a match on a dating app. You haven't met in person yet, but the conversation feels warm and personal. One evening, she says something has come up and asks you to pay for something online right away — nothing large, just enough to feel like a small favour between two people who trust each other. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: NDTV, Sept 2 — a Bengaluru man described losing money after a dating-app match asked him to 'pay online.' This online-payment-to-an-unmet-match mechanism is distinct from the dating-app meetup robbery covered on 2026-08-30 (a physical lure to an isolated spot) and hasn't otherwise been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: You've never met her in person, video-called only briefly and never for long, and every time you suggest meeting up something gets in the way. She's never asked for money before, so this feels like an exception rather than a pattern.

choices.text: Decline to send any money, and treat the request itself as a signal to verify who you're actually talking to — a reverse image search of her photos, a video call on your terms, or a suggestion to meet in a public place.
choices.feedback: Correct. The very first request for money from someone you haven't met in person — however small or reasonable it sounds — is the standard trigger point for a romance scam, exactly as in today's case. Verifying identity first (reverse image search, an unscripted video call, insisting on meeting publicly) costs you nothing and exposes a fake profile immediately.

choices.text: Pay the small amount this one time since she's never asked before and the relationship otherwise feels genuine.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Scammers deliberately start with a small, reasonable-sounding ask to establish that you'll pay — the amounts escalate once the first payment goes through, which is exactly the pattern the Bengaluru victim described. 'She's never asked before' is not evidence of trust; it's often the setup.

choices.text: Ask her to prove her identity with a selfie holding a handwritten note, then pay once she sends it.
choices.feedback: Risky. A selfie is easy to stage or reuse from other photos and proves nothing about who's really behind the account. It creates a false sense of verification while still ending in the same payment a scammer wants.

choices.text: Block and report the profile immediately without any further conversation.
choices.feedback: Risky. This avoids the immediate loss but assumes bad intent without checking — a small number of genuine people do ask for help early in a relationship. The safer middle path is to verify identity and insist on meeting in person before any money changes hands, not to end contact on the first ask.

takeaways: Never send money to someone you haven't met in person, no matter how small the amount or how long you've been chatting — this is the exact mechanism in today's Bengaluru case.
A reverse image search (Google Lens or TinEye) on a match's profile photos takes under a minute and catches most stolen-photo romance scam profiles.
Report suspected romance scam profiles to the National Cyber Crime helpline (1930 or cybercrime.gov.in) — the earlier it's reported, the better the chance of tracing the payment.

quiz.question: Which regulatory body has approved new DTG trains for Namma Metro to help ease overcrowding, per today's news?
quiz.why: CMRS (Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety) certifies new rolling stock as safe before it can be inducted into passenger service.

quiz.question: Estonia's defence minister resigned this week amid fallout over a Rs 770 crore deal with an Indian firm for what?
quiz.why: The controversy centred on an ammunition supply deal, per Firstpost's reporting on the minister's exit.

quiz.question: What kind of satellite did ISRO successfully launch this week, per today's news?
quiz.why: EOS-05 is an Earth observation satellite, part of ISRO's series of satellites used for environmental and resource monitoring.

quiz.question: What is the sanctioned strength of judges (including the Chief Justice) in India's Supreme Court?
quiz.why: Parliament raised the Supreme Court's sanctioned strength from 31 to 34 judges through a 2019 amendment to the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act.

quiz.question: Which is India's largest state by land area?
quiz.why: Rajasthan covers roughly 342,000 sq km, ahead of Madhya Pradesh, and includes most of the Thar Desert.
